Jasmine — initial findings after quick checks:
- No model rollout recorded in control plane for CobaltHealth (model pinned to open-llm-cobalt-v2.1).
- GPU utilization across their pool at the time shows moderate, not saturated (avg 62%), but one host shows repeated memcpy stalls and elevated kernel retries.
- Disk IO on that host shows occasional NVMe latency spikes coincident with the P95 jump.
- Network starved briefly (burst queue) between 08:48-08:52; packet retransmits in pcap match that window.

Plan A (fast): remove the hot host from pool, fail over traffic to spare nodes (we have burst capacity in their Dedicated profile). This should drop error rate within 5–8 minutes.
Plan B (next 3 hours): collect full kernel traces, run nvme SMART, and if NVMe is root cause, replace the device in maintenance window.

I'll start failover now and report back in 6 minutes.

-Marissa
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Dedicated

Subject: Incident summary and exec ask — CobaltHealth VPC variance (RESOLVED)

Team, final update and exec note for leadership:

Timeline (short):
- 2027-06-28 08:48 PDT: CobaltHealth reports P95 jump and 5xx.
- 08:55 PDT: SRE removed bad host from pool; error rate dropped to ~0.15% within 6 minutes.
- 09:10 PDT: Warmup priming completed on spares; tail latency returned to baseline for steady traffic.
- 11:05 PDT: CobaltHealth batch window ran; no repeat spike recorded.

Root cause: intermittent NVMe firmware bug on one appliance host caused I/O stalls and blocked the local inference runtime during certain KV cache flush paths. Packet retransmits amplified tail effects.

Remediation applied:
- Immediate: host removed and replaced with spare; automatic rebalancing allowed warm cache priming.
- Short-term: scheduled NVMe firmware upgrade on their appliance fleet (maintenance window 2027-07-02 02:00–04:00 PDT).
- Medium-term: added host-level disk-health telemetry to our customer incident dashboard and automated host removal on NVMe SMART threshold breach.

Customer impact: minimal after failover (one delayed batch run start, no data loss). SLA risk: none after mitigation.

Exec ask: please approve an exception to schedule a coordinated overnight maintenance for CobaltHealth (07/02 02:00–04:00 PDT) — this requires a one-time dedicated engineering shift and a firmware image distribution via our Private deployment pipeline. Estimated engineering cost: 6 engineer-hours (SRE + infra + account).

I've attached a 1-page action summary for the execs and the CSV/pcap we used in triage.

-Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
